title: BAL@ATL-card
universal_lens: The Ballistics Window unifies biophysical drag, roster availability matrices, and spatial tracking metrics into a single high-dimensional state vector. It models the game as a constrained optimization problem where environmental perturbations shift the expected value of discrete action-space trajectories.
gsi_mapping: GSI ingests the stadium air density and injury status flags as priors in a hierarchical Bayesian model. Conformal prediction intervals are dynamically adjusted using live Next Gen Stats separation metrics to bound the uncertainty of player-specific outcome distributions.
gse_mapping: GSE translates the primitive operators into real-time Markov Decision Processes. The engine evaluates how wind vectors and defensive line rotation changes alter the transition probabilities between offensive play-calling states, optimizing for maximum expected yardage gain.

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \rho (air density) in kg/m^3; v_{wind} (wind speed) in km/h; \Delta d (distance shift) in meters.
primitives.assumptions: Standard projectile motion with quadratic drag coefficient; constant microclimate within the domed stadium during the event window.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Model fails if extreme turbulence or sudden pressure drops invalidate the steady-state aerodynamic assumptions.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE physics engine's ballistic solver, adjusting the terminal velocity and range parameters for all kicking and passing actions.

primitives.name: Defensive Rotation Leverage Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: AVAILABILITY: Za'Darius Smith (ATL) listed QUESTIONABLE [docs/data-sources/research/2026-10-13/injuries/espn_nfl_injuries_week6.json] -> unit rotation depth changes at that position -> snap share and pressure/scheme leverage shift toward the opponent's strength 3.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P(status) (probability of participation) dimensionless; \Delta SS (snap share delta) in percentage points; L (leverage index) dimensionless.
primitives.assumptions: Replacement units exhibit strictly lower efficiency metrics; coaching staff optimizes scheme around the remaining personnel constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the backup unit possesses equivalent or superior pass-rush metrics, neutralizing the expected leverage shift.

layer2.mapping: Feeds the GSI Bayesian network to update the posterior distribution of quarterback pressure rates and subsequent negative play probability.
layer2.telemetry: Observed pressure rate and sack conversion percentage against the opposing quarterback.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins by establishing the baseline physical state of the environment, specifically the air density and wind vectors at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. These continuous variables define the boundary conditions for all ballistic events, creating an initial perturbation to standard sea-level projection models. Simultaneously, we introduce discrete stochastic variables representing player availability. The questionable status of key defensive linemen acts as a binary switch that alters the underlying topology of the defensive formation space. By integrating these two distinct domains—continuous physics and discrete roster constraints—we construct a composite state vector. This vector is then refined using high-frequency tracking data, such as Run Yards Over Expected (RYOE). The RYOE metric serves as a ground-truth calibration, proving that the theoretical advantages derived from roster shifts are materializing in actual spatial dominance. The final operator emerges from the confluence of these layers: a dynamic expectation of field positioning and scoring probability that accounts for both the literal flight of the ball and the structural integrity of the opposing defense. Failure modes arise when the discrete injury reports do not translate to expected snap share reductions, or when environmental conditions fluctuate rapidly outside the modeled steady-state.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This analytical framework inherits its lineage from early 20th-century ballistics research combined with mid-century operations research. The integration of environmental drag coefficients mirrors the work of physicists modeling artillery trajectories under varying atmospheric pressures. Meanwhile, the incorporation of personnel availability and spatial efficiency traces back to linear programming and resource allocation theories developed during the Manhattan Project. Modern sports analytics merely applies these rigorous mathematical traditions to the bounded geometry of the American football field.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the opposing head coach as a rational actor operating under severe information asymmetry and time constraints. When a premier edge rusher is listed as questionable, the opposing coordinator must probabilistically hedge their protection schemes, allocating additional resources to blind-side protection. Our primitives exploit this cognitive load by quantifying the exact cost of that hedging. We anticipate that the human decision-maker will over-index on preventing catastrophic sacks, thereby opening high-value spatial vulnerabilities in the secondary that our tracking metrics are designed to exploit.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict anti-collinearity veto is applied if the environmental perturbations (e.g., wind) perfectly align with the roster deficiencies, creating a degenerate state where the outcome becomes trivially predictable. Furthermore, we enforce a leakage veto: if the DFS market has already fully priced in the absence of the edge rusher, the alpha generated by the Defensive Rotation Leverage Kernel is nullified. The system must continuously monitor the Pinnacle guest lines to ensure that our derived spatial advantages have not been arbitraged away by sharper market participants before the snap.
